data.name: Lopamudra
data.gender_notes: Lopamudra is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Lopamudra is a celestial nymph who is said to have been the wife of the sage Agastya. She is described as a beautiful, fertile woman who abounds in water, and is often depicted carrying a jug or standing near a river. The name Lopamudra carries the meaning “Fertile, Abounding in Water” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lopamudra usually hope their child will grow to embody fertile, abounding in water and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine energy, abundance, and fertility.
data.etymology: Lopamudra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fertile, Abounding in Water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lopamudra total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

She is often depicted in various forms of art, literature, and architecture, particularly in the eastern part of India where the sage Agastya is revered.
data.spiritual_significance: Lopamudra represents the divine feminine or Shakti, the creative and nurturing force of the universe. She embodies the water element, which is essential for creation and sustenance. Her name "Lopamudra" signifies one who is "filled with mudra" or signs or symbols of the divine. Thus, she is a symbol of divine grace, fertility, and spiritual fulfilment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lopamudra: Abounding in Desire and Grace. A name signifying the embodiment of deep longing and exquisite beauty.

vedic_reference.note: Lopamudra was a courtesan of ancient India. She is best known for her role as the protagonist in the epic Mahabharata. She was a great scholar and was the wife of King Yudhishthira. Lopamudra is also known for her wisdom and her knowledge of the Vedas.

historical_references.reference: Lopamudra was a queen of King Sahasrarjuna of Haihayas in ancient India, mentioned in the epic Mahabharata.
